canonical_statement: The study evaluated platelet aggregation responses to multiple agonists in patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia receiving tyrosine kinase inhibitors to investigate a possible primary-hemostasis defect associated with TKI therapy.

Ninety-one patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia were evaluated; the study group included 20 receiving imatinib, 1 newly diagnosed patient, and 70 patients treated after imatinib failure with nilotinib (n=9), bosutinib (n=32), or dasatinib (n=29).

population.label: Patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia evaluated in the study

canonical_statement: Patients were followed with complete blood counts and basic coagulation studies (PT, aPTT, and fibrinogen) every 3 to 6 months; informed consent and institutional review board approval were reported.

Light-transmittance aggregometry was performed within 4 hours in citrated platelet-rich plasma using weak and strong ADP, arachidonic acid, collagen, epinephrine, and low- and high-dose ristocetin stimulation with predefined abnormality cutoffs.

For PFA-100 time-course testing, normal-donor whole blood was incubated with dasatinib or imatinib 400 nM for 0, 30, 60, and 120 minutes before collagen/epinephrine and collagen/ADP closure-time testing; the Methods specify a single donor known to respond to epinephrine.
At the time of aggregation testing, 4 patients were off TKI therapy and 87 were receiving dasatinib (n=27), bosutinib (n=32), imatinib (n=19), or nilotinib (n=9).

population.label: CML-CP cohort at platelet aggregation testing

canonical_statement: The cohort had a median age of 54 years (range 21-80), median WBC 6.1 x10^9/L (range 2.1-58.5), hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL (range 8.2-15.4), and platelet count 227 x10^9/L (range 80-746); 74 of 91 patients (81%) had platelets above 150 x10^9/L.

population.label: CML-CP cohort at baseline laboratory characterization

canonical_statement: Abnormal coagulation testing was observed in 3 patients, all receiving imatinib with concomitant warfarin, and the abnormality was prolonged prothrombin time.

population.label: CML-CP study cohort assessed for coagulation abnormalities

exposures.details: Three patients with abnormal coagulation tests were receiving both agents.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Abnormal coagulation tests were observed in only 3 patients on imatinib concomitantly receiving warfarin, who exhibited prolonged PT.

canonical_statement: Among the remaining 88 patients, median PT was 11.1 seconds (range 9.8-13.1), median aPTT 28.5 seconds (range 21-33.9), and median fibrinogen 470 mg/dL (range 336-700), which the authors interpreted as suggesting intact secondary hemostasis.

population.label: Patients excluding the 3 imatinib-plus-warfarin cases with prolonged PT

canonical_statement: Twelve of 91 patients (13%) were receiving aspirin and exhibited faulty arachidonic-acid-induced platelet aggregation.

canonical_statement: All 4 patients who were off TKI therapy had normal platelet aggregation.

canonical_statement: At aggregation testing, 46 patients (51%) had complete cytogenetic response, 7 (8%) partial cytogenetic response, 10 (11%) minor cytogenetic response, 18 (19%) complete hematologic response, and 10 (11%) no response; the complete-cytogenetic-response group included 15 major and 2 complete molecular responses.

canonical_statement: No patient had active bleeding at the time platelet aggregation was tested.
Among 27 dasatinib-treated patients not receiving aspirin, 23 (85%) had reduced epinephrine-induced platelet aggregation.

canonical_statement: Two patients with markedly abnormal epinephrine-induced aggregation while receiving dasatinib (22% and 17%, respectively) normalized their platelet aggregation tests after switching to bosutinib 500 mg/day.

Figure 1 reports that dasatinib was more frequently associated with epinephrine-induced aggregation defects than imatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib (P<.001, one-way ANOVA); for arachidonic-acid defects, dasatinib differed from nilotinib and bosutinib (P<.001) but not imatinib (P=.55).

In Table 1, dasatinib 400 nM increased collagen/epinephrine PFA-100 closure time from 126 seconds at time 0 to >300 seconds at 30 minutes, 297 seconds at 60 minutes, and >300 seconds at 120 minutes, while collagen/ADP closure times remained 77-87 seconds.

In Table 1, imatinib 400 nM did not prolong collagen/epinephrine PFA-100 closure time across 0, 30, 60, and 120 minutes (86, 89, 94, and 70 seconds, respectively); collagen/ADP values were 93, 126, 114, and 131 seconds.

The authors concluded that dasatinib inhibits platelet function by impairing arachidonic-acid- and epinephrine-induced aggregation; they stated that this effect is not related to thrombocytopenia or clonal hematopoiesis and may account in part for bleeding in dasatinib-treated patients.
The authors concluded that impaired arachidonic-acid-induced platelet aggregation can also occur with imatinib, although less frequently than with dasatinib.
The mechanism by which dasatinib induces platelet dysfunction was unknown, and the authors stated that the mechanism of the platelet dysfunction warrants further investigation.
